summary:
NASA Mission Gallery is an interactive journey through space exploration, from the Moon and Mars to asteroids, the outer planets, and worlds beyond our solar system. We developed a web experience that brings NASA mission records to life through visual stories, interactive 3D spacecraft models, timelines, and short challenges.

Each mission invites visitors to explore the problem scientists wanted to solve, the spacecraft built for the journey, and what the mission discovered. Readers can also explore detailed articles and follow links to the original NASA sources.

The project makes a large collection of scientific information easier to navigate and understand. By connecting discoveries with the people, machines, and decisions behind them, it helps students and curious explorers see space exploration as an ongoing human story—and encourages them to keep asking questions.
details:
NASA Mission Gallery is a curiosity-driven web experience that makes space exploration easier to discover and understand. Instead of asking visitors to navigate a large archive first, it guides them through missions using a simple question: What was the challenge, and how did this mission help us learn more?

Each chapter combines a mission story, a timeline, spacecraft visuals, and a short interactive challenge. Visitors can explore a mission at their own pace, then open a full article when they want to go deeper. The articles use clear sections, shorter paragraphs, and a navigation index to make longer material easier to read. Links to NASA’s original records give curious readers a path to the source.

Accessibility and ease of use shaped the experience. The site uses readable text, clear navigation, keyboard-accessible controls, and support for reduced motion. Interactive 3D models help visitors examine spacecraft, while images and written descriptions provide context throughout the journey.

We built the project with Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Three.js. A Rust scraper collects mission information from NASA’s National Space Science Data Center, which we organize into stories and learning activities.

Our goal is to make NASA’s mission history welcoming to students, educators, and anyone curious about space. By pairing reliable information with an inviting way to explore, we hope to turn a moment of curiosity into a lasting interest in science and discovery.
